sections.title: Why this policy exists
paragraphs: This policy forms part of the Terms for Alex Orr's current personal All Seeing Eye installation. The main risk for an open-source intelligence tool is misuse against private individuals, so these rules apply to everything you do with the installation and its outputs.

sections.title: You must not
paragraphs: Use the installation only for lawful, proportionate research. In particular, you must not:
items: target, profile, locate or monitor private individuals
stalk, harass, threaten or dox anyone
carry out unauthorised surveillance or credential theft
breach the Computer Misuse Act 1990 or other computer misuse law that applies to you, export controls or sanctions
circumvent a source's terms, access controls or rate limits, or redistribute licensed data beyond what its licence allows
use outputs as the sole basis for decisions affecting individuals' rights, or for discriminatory decisions
upload material you lack authority to use or send to the selected providers

sections.title: How to report misuse
paragraphs: Report suspected misuse of the installation or its outputs to alexorr@yahoo.co.uk. Say which page, report or account is involved and what you saw. Do not include passwords or private research material.

sections.title: What happens to accounts that break this policy
paragraphs: The operator may restrict access to investigate misuse or protect the service. An administrator can deactivate an account, which stops it signing in and ends its access to the installation, while personal-data requests continue to be handled through the published procedure.

paragraphs.pending: Any further consequences, such as notice to the account holder, an appeal route or referral of unlawful use to the authorities, need the operator's decision.
